title: Fitbit Versa 4 bundle hits its lowest price since February
summary: The Fitbit Versa 4 bundle drops to $159.99 on Amazon, with GPS, heart-rate tracking, and useful extras included.
body: The Fitbit Versa 4 is built for people who care more about fitness and daily health tracking than loading up a watch with tons of apps, and there’s a nice deal on Amazon right now. This bundle gives you the Fitbit watch itself plus a few useful extras, so it’s a good way to get started with less extra shopping. See the deal at Amazon

title: Garmin CIRQA adds vibration alerts for calls and texts in latest update
summary: The change is part of firmware update version 4.20.
body: TL;DR The Garmin CIRQA Smart Band now has vibration notifications for calls and text messages. The feature was one requested by CIRQA customers on Garmin’s forums. The change comes with firmware update 4.20, which also brings three other new features to the CIRQA. Screenless fitness trackers are becoming increasingly popular and some of that is owed to them not being a constant distraction like smartwatches are. The Fitbit Air , WHOOP , and the like remain firmly fitness-focused and don’t notify wearers about incoming phone calls and text messages on their phones. Garmin’s CIRQA Smart Band was the same, but the company just reversed course with its version 4.20 update. Listed in the changelog for the firmware update from version 3.0 to 4.0 is “Support vibration for smart notifications/incoming calls” (via Gadgets & Wearables ). However, the FAQ page for CIRQA still claims, “The CIRQA smart band does not vibrate for text messages, phone calls, or other smartphone notifications.”

title: Google isn’t ruling out this major Pixel Watch feature for the Fitbit Edge
summary: The tracker has the right sensors, but Google's plans are still taking shape.
body: TL;DR Google has told Android Authority that it’s looking to bring sleep breathing quality to the Fitbit Edge. The tracker already supports blood pressure and insulin resistance trends through Google Health Premium, but it still lacks the sleep feature. Unlike the Fitbit Air, which Google says will get the feature soon, support for the Fitbit Edge doesn’t seem guaranteed yet. The Fitbit Edge has plenty going for it as Google’s long-awaited successor to the Charge lineup. It packs an AMOLED display, built-in GPS, advanced health sensors, and even a user-replaceable battery , a first for Fitbit. But despite all that hardware, the $180 tracker is missing one of Google’s newest health insights. Fortunately, the company has now given us reason to believe that might change.
